notes:
Lead source: inbound self-serve signup (trial credits used). Signed up 2026-03-01, onboarding flow completed but ran into streaming + function-calling issues while wiring to product front-end.

Discovery call 2026-03-09 (30m) w/ AE Maya + SE Liam + engineering lead (Nadia). Notes:
- Customer use-case: in-app assistant for shoppers: streaming chat bubbles + ability to call product search API (tool) and return structured JSON for UI to render product cards.
- Target SLOs: 150ms first token, <800ms average response for simple lookups; bursts to ~20 req/s during campaigns. SMB but sensitivity to latency.
- Current integration: frontend expects strict camelCase JSON with keys: {productId, title, priceCents, imageUrl, snippet}. They use a small parser that fails if trailing commas/partial chunks are present.

Problems observed:
- When stream mode enabled, frontend assembly falters because model emits incremental tokens and sometimes includes explanatory text before the JSON payload ("Here's what I found: {...}"). Parser chokes. ("We only need the JSON object — why is there prose?")
- Function calling attempted but model sometimes returns plain assistant text instead of calling the function schema, or returns object with snake_case keys and missing required fields.
- Schema mismatch: their function_schema marked some fields as required but model returned them as strings instead of numbers (priceCents as "$12.99" vs integer cents). Frontend had no fallback.
- Intermittent malformed JSON in stream: truncated arrays, trailing commas during re-rolls; assembling tokens into a valid JSON requires heuristics they don't want.

What customer has tried:
- Toggled between streaming=true/false. Non-streaming works more reliably but > latency target.
- Added soft prompt to ask model to "only output valid JSON, no extra prose" — reduced but didn't eliminate cases.
- Quick mapping layer in frontend to normalize keys (snake_case -> camelCase) — still brittle when required keys missing.

SE notes (Liam):
- Likely teachable via stricter function schema + example invocation; recommend using function_call explicit mode if they need deterministic function invocation.
- For streaming use-case: suggest sending stream for tokens but emit only after function call finished (i.e., use function calling to get structured data, then stream rendered chat). Alternative: stream with 'json_mode' enforcement and bracket-counting on client to wait until top-level object closed before parsing.

Open items / blockers:
- Customer asks for snippet: minimal request payload that guarantees function-call return with correct types + streaming-friendly behavior.
- Billing/quotas: want clarif on free-trial conversion and estimated monthly cost for 10k messages / month.
- Security: SAML SSO will be required for teams >50 — they will want SOC2 checklist (send security FAQ).
